title: Stowaway oncall transcript
content:
Context / intent:
This is a very rough pass — quick transcript-style handoff for the next person taking the late-east shift. Not a final runbook; copy important steps into the canonical runbook under Confluence later.

Current state (as of 2026-03-13 09:15 PT):
- Cluster: prod-inference-us-west (primary pool).
- Incident ballast: memory pressure on serving nodes observed overnight, intermittent OOM kills on p3d-sidecar-02.
- Rolling restarts in progress (started 03-13 01:40 PT) to pick up kernel patch & new oomd tune. ~60% complete.
- Canary traffic is healthy; fallback routing to cpu-fallback group activated for a subset of low-priority model routes.

Top items for next shift:
1) Watch for repeating OOM pattern after restarts finish. Grep logs for the pattern: `OOM killed process|signal 9` across the last 4 hours.
   - Command: `gcloud compute ssh svc-prod-ops --zone=us-west1-b --command "sudo journalctl -u inference-worker -n 500 | grep -E 'OOM|Killed process'"`
2) If OOMs continue, temporarily scale up memory-limited pool by +2 nodes (see playbook quick steps below).
3) Monitor routing errors: any >1% 5xxs on /v1/generate for model-redwood-7b in the past 10m -> trigger paging and escalate to oncall-eng.

Recent mitigations applied (do not revert unless instructed):
- Kernel parameter `vm.min_free_kbytes` bumped to 262144 on p3d nodes (applied via automation bundle `ops-config` PR #422).
- oomd thresholds relaxed for cache-heavy workers to avoid noisy restarts.
- Canary routing enabled for fallback-cpu-group for non-SLA routes (config id: route-fallback-2026-03-13).

Temporary hotfix: memory spike workaround (how to run quickly)
- Use when you see steady growth >80% mem + swap spike across all pods on a node.
- Steps: 
  1. Drain the node (cordon + drain, but keep evictions graceful): `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`
  2. SSH into node, run `sudo systemctl restart inference-worker` once drained containers are gone.
  3. After restart, monitor heap usage of the top process: `ps aux --sort=-rss | head -n 10` and `kubectl logs -n inference <pod> --tail=200`
  4. If process still grows quickly, scale deployment: `kubectl scale deploy model-7b-worker --replicas=$(($(kubectl get deploy model-7b-worker -o jsonpath='{.status.replicas}') + 2))`

Quick checks (first 10 minutes):
- k8s nodes: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` (check Ready status and memory alloc)
- pods in inference ns: `kubectl get pods -n inference --sort-by=.status.startTime`\- check for CrashLoopBackOff or OOMKilled
- route health: hit `/health/route/model-redwood-7b` via internal loadbalancer (curl from jump host)
- logs: `kail -n inference -l app=model-7b | grep -i 'ERROR\|OOM'`

Notes to self / open questions:
- Why did the older kernel param set fail to propagate to p3d-sidecar-02? Automation shows success but node still reported old vm.min_free_kbytes during early morning checks. Might be an ordering/timing race with the node reboot cycle.
- We should add a dedicated memory watermark alert for worker-side caches (threshold suggestion: 78% resident mem for >5m).
- Need to validate that fallback routing does not exceed cost budget when enabled long-term. Put an action item on product-ops to sign off.

Things I did not have time to finish:
- Draft a small test harness to repro the mem growth with the new kernel setting. Left a TODO in my laptop: `~/tmp/mem-repro/README.md`
- Update Confluence runbook; added a stub note in the ticket SRE-913.

Escalation contacts:
- Primary oncall eng: Samir Desai (pager)
- Secondary: Yvonne Zhang (Slack @yzhang)
- SRE manager: Marcus Li (macli@redwood.ai)

Immediate comms guidance (if public-facing latency page needed):
- Template: short ack + mitigation + ETA for fix. Example: "We're investigating increased memory pressure on inference nodes that is impacting some requests. We've applied mitigations and are performing rolling restarts — service remains available with some degraded performance for lower-priority requests. We'll post updates every 30 minutes."

Housekeeping (write down before you log):
- If you add any remediation steps to this doc, prepend with timestamp and your initials.
- Create a Confluence update after incident stabilized: page `SRE -> Incidents -> 2026-03-13 prod-inference-memory` and link to SRE-913.

End of transcript — TL;DR:
- Memory pressure caused OOMs overnight. Rolling restarts + kernel tweak applied. Watch for recurrence and be prepared to scale worker replicas or keep fallback routing active.

-- LK 2026-03-13 09:13 PT
